newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Prague bourse extends losses, mkt sentiment bearish.
newsitem.headline: Prague bourse extends losses, mkt sentiment bearish.

text.p: The Prague Strock Exchange extended its downtrend to seven consecutive sessions on Wednesday, as ailing blue chips continued to fall on sagging investor confidence.
Several financial sector issues lost ground to pull the PX50 index down 1.5 points, or 0.27 percent, to 548.2, while the Reuters RPIX index fell three points to 1,111.
And analyst predictions do not bode well for the beleaguered bourse for the short-term.
"The market is suffering and I don't think we will se a change in its fortunes this week for sure," said one local analyst.
Overall, 194 shares lost, 143 rose, and 72 held steady on volume of 981,224 shares. Total turnover was 881.3 million crowns.
In an attempt to boost activity on the bourse, the PSE said it would add three issues to its continuous trading session.
The bourse statement said engineering concern Skoda, bank IPB, investment fund SPIF Cesky would be added to the continuous session as of November 4.
Seven equity issues and two bonds are currently traded in the continuous session.
The PSE also said it had also decided to merge the second and third trading groups within the bourse's free market, effective January 1.
Stocks in the second group have their prices fixed once a session, while the shares in the third group have their prices fixed twice weekly. Prices in the merged group will be fixed daily.
"This will immediately bring a rise in oversight and will be a clear signal on the standardisation of the market to foreign investors," the PSE said.
